title: Close your laptop. Keep DeepSeek Harness working on Blaxel.
summary: Move a DeepSeek Harness session to Blaxel, keep the agent working independently, then review changes and bring the conversation and code back locally.
body_markdown:
Your coding agent is halfway through a task, and you need to leave. Move the session to a Blaxel sandbox, close your laptop, and let the agent keep working. When you are back, review the changes and bring the conversation and code home.


Cloud session handoff in the[DeepSeek Harness integration](https://github.com/blaxel-ai/deepseek-harness-blaxel-sandbox) moves your current project and conversation into an independent, private agent host. The cloud runs the model requests and tools, so progress no longer depends on keeping your original DeepSeek process alive.


## Take the current task with you


We used Invoice Desk, a small billing application, to test the journey. It already exported invoices as CSV. Our next task was to add **All, Paid, and Pending filters** and make the export follow the selected view.


The conversation began locally with an implementation plan. We then wrote the next prompt and left it unsent. Selecting **Move to Blaxel** carried the project, conversation, and draft into the cloud page, ready to continue the same task.


*The next instruction arrives with the conversation. Send it when you are ready to continue on Blaxel.*


The plugin includes uncommitted edits and unignored source files. Git-ignored paths, common credential files, and private keys stay out of the snapshot. The launch panel shows workspace preparation and cloud startup; wait for the cloud page to be ready before leaving.


## Let the agent keep working


We suspended the dedicated local DeepSeek host and then sent the implementation prompt from the already-open cloud page. New file reads, edits, and test commands ran remotely while the original host remained paused.


The first agent response needed corrections: an unavailable fetch-library import, the temporary server's port, and HTTP assertions that included navigation labels. Follow-ups fixed those issues using Node's built-in fetch. The completed change passed thirteen tests, including status filtering, input immutability, and the HTTP routes.


That is the useful boundary: you can continue the work, inspect progress, and send another instruction from the cloud conversation. **Copy private link** provides private browser access without exposing the sandbox publicly. Treat the link as a credential, and reopen the session from the original computer to renew expired access.


## Review the work before it comes home


On the original computer with DeepSeek Harness running, select **Move back to local** . The review lists changed files and shows the actual patch before you choose **Apply changes and move back** .


The transfer checks the patch against your current local files. It returns the conversation and pending draft, restores the original local permissions, and stops the sandbox after files and history are durable locally.


We tested the result locally: thirteen tests passed, and independent HTTP checks returned three invoices for All, two for Paid, and one for Pending. The application now offers the filters alongside Export CSV.


*The returned project includes the working filter and its tests, ready for local development.*


## Move the same session again


After the first return, we added a local README checkpoint and moved the conversation again. The second cloud task documented the filters while preserving that checkpoint. Its return review made the small addition visible before applying it.


*Cloud changes and newer local work meet at an explicit review step.*


We also tested an interrupted return after restarting the local host, and separately introduced a conflicting local edit. The return kept both copies, retained the cloud session, and saved a recovery patch. After resolving the conflict, retrying brought the work back successfully.


Handoff and return are explicit transfers. Reopening an existing sandbox reconnects to its current files; it does not upload newer local edits. Choose a sandbox lifetime that leaves time to return your work. This walkthrough used one hour.


Independent cloud execution requires a portable API key for the selected native pi-ai or DeepSeek model. That key enters the private cloud host, where the agent has full VM access without per-tool approval. Blaxel credentials remain local. Laptop-only endpoints, local OAuth grants, external skills, and host MCP configuration do not migrate.


Install the current cloud-capable plugin release with the tutorial's` @latest` commands. Follow the[DeepSeek Harness tutorial](https://docs.blaxel.ai/Tutorials/DeepSeek-Harness) for installation, the copyable Invoice Desk prompts, and the complete local-to-cloud-to-local walkthrough.
